nodes.text: scripts/setup.sh is the single setup command: it takes a machine with nothing installed to passing checks, and is safe to re-run.
CI runs exactly scripts/setup.sh on fresh macOS and Linux runners; there is no CI-only setup.
CI passes GITHUB_TOKEN so mise's downloads from GitHub are not rate-limited.
say prints a bold step line and die prints a red error and exits 1, so every failure stops setup with a reason.
On a Mac without the Command Line Tools, git is installed by softwareupdate under sudo; a marker file in /tmp makes softwareupdate offer the tools, and the newest label is picked.
The check is xcode-select -p rather than running git, because /usr/bin/git exists on every Mac as a stub that opens Apple's installer dialog.
After that step git must actually run; on Linux it is expected to come from the system package manager.
mise is pinned to MISE_VERSION and downloaded from that GitHub release into ~/.local/bin, only when the installed version is not exactly that one.
Each platform's mise tarball is pinned by SHA-256 in the script itself, so the download is trusted only if it is byte-for-byte the file the repo expects; a mismatch stops setup.
OS and CPU are mapped to mise's release asset names (macos/linux, arm64/x64); anything else stops setup.
Tool versions (node, gh) are declared in mise.toml, and mise install installs exactly those, from the repo root, after the file is marked trusted.
npm packages install exactly as the lockfile says, through npm ci in the mise task `install`.
Installed packages (node_modules/) are never committed.
scratch/ is a temporary local working folder that is never committed. It is a working convention, not part of the product.
INTERACTIVE is set only when stdin is a terminal and CI is unset; it gates every step that would edit your shell config or wait for you.
In an interactive zsh or bash, a `mise activate` line is appended to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc once, so node, gh and mise are on PATH in new terminals.
gh logs in through the browser only when it is not logged in and the run is interactive; otherwise setup carries on, because building and testing never need GitHub.
Setup ends with `mise run check`, which runs typecheck and tests; a failure there fails setup.
The only test is a smoke test proving the TypeScript toolchain runs; tsconfig is strict and checks src and test without emitting.
src/graph.ts defines an understanding graph of the code a PR touches, as it stands at the PR's head: a list of nodes and a list of edges, where node order is reading order.
A node is an id unique within its graph, text saying what is true about some code (as long as it needs to be), and the locations of that code.
An edge says `to` helps explain `from`, with an optional free-text note; there are no edge types.
A location reuses GitHub's PR review-comment fields unchanged: path, side (LEFT = base, so deleted code; RIGHT = head), an optional start_line and the last line.
